scenarios.procedure: Run the same preparation again over the finished reference library.
scenarios.expected: Ready again, no step runs again, and the identity equals the reference.

scenarios.procedure: Prepare from nothing; the analyzer pauses inside the broadcast analysis after writing 300 bytes of its map, by which time the WCAG analysis has committed. SIGKILL the process group there, then run the same command again.
scenarios.expected: While killed the receipt is not ready and nothing is listed. The restart reuses the committed WCAG analysis, redoes the torn one, is ready, and its identity equals the reference.

scenarios.procedure: From the finished reference, delete the WCAG safe master so its rendition step has to run again. An ffmpeg wrapper writes half of the new master at the real path and stops; SIGKILL the process group there, then run the same command with the real ffmpeg.
scenarios.expected: No record vouches for the half-written master, nothing is ready while the run is dead, and the restart rebuilds the rendition, is ready, and equals the reference.

limitations: No power was cut. Durability rests on fsync, and on macOS F_FULLFSYNC, as the operating system and filesystem implement them; these runs used one machine and one filesystem.

Every scenario but the last uses the fake analyzer, whose flagged spans are scripted. Hashing, source binding, Ed25519 signing, rendering, HLS packaging and the verification gates are real, so outcomes show the pipeline's recovery and publication gates, not flash measurement.
Sweep kills are timed, so where each one lands varies between runs; each landing point is recorded.

A SIGKILL sent only to the Python process, not its group, can leave an ffmpeg or analyzer child writing until it finishes. Such late writes can only cause a mismatch and a rebuild: verification refuses bytes that change under it and a receipt must name exactly the bytes verification recorded. That case is covered by the in-process tests, not by a scenario here.
Locks are advisory flock locks on one machine. Work directories shared between machines, for example over NFS, are not serialized.
Comparisons assume ffmpeg and x264 produce the same bytes for the same input on one machine, which these runs observed; a different build or thread count can change encoded bytes between runs.
Work directories prepared before this change carry no output hashes, so their first run redoes every step. With the real analyzer that issues new maps with a new created_utc and signature.
